title: How to Choose an International Payment Gateway in India: Fees, Settlement and Checklist (2027)
summary: Compare international payment gateway fees, settlement time, RBI authorisation and export documents in India. Use a practical checklist before choosing.

Toggle


### Key Takeaways


- Always look to see if the RBI has authorised the provider first. RBI has to approve the non-bank provider handling cross-border payment aggregation, and an Indian exporter requires inward-payment coverage.
- Check the full cost, don’t just look at the headline rate. 2.99% per successful international card transaction, with no setup fee, is Cashfree’s listed standard rate. Any international payment gateway should have its GST treatment and conversion margin written down.
- Make sure that the settlement timeline is included in the contract. As far as timelines for cross-border settlements are concerned, RBI does not specify a universal T+N cycle; as far as non-INR settlement is concerned, it is allowed only for Indian exporters that the aggregator has onboarded directly, subject to the supported arrangement.
- Verify the export documents. Each international payment gateway may have its own remittance document, therefore see if your AD bank and accountant accept it for the purpose required.
- Do not exceed the transaction limit. The RBI has capped inward and outward transactions processed through a PA-CB to a maximum of ₹25 lakh each.


International payments are a necessity for Indian businesses to offer overseas customers a payment system that allows them to pay using their own payment methods and their own currency. With regards to international payments, selecting the right payment gateway is crucial.


Whether you are a freelancer, exporter, SaaS business, or an e-commerce brand, selecting the right international payment gateway helps avoid unnecessary costs, delays or compliance issues.


[International payment gateways](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-an-international-payment-gateway/) facilitate payments by international cards and can convert the currency to INR, which can be credited to your Indian bank account. An example of this is Cashfree, which accepts international card payments in 140+ currencies and settles them in INR. For an international payment gateway comparison in India, compare providers on the basis of:


- Approval by the RBI
- Cost
- Settlement
- Export documents and limits


##


Step 1: Start with RBI Authorisation


Before you consider the first price, ensure that the provider is permitted to process cross-border payments. These cross-border aggregation services are regulated by the RBI as Payment Aggregators–Cross Border (PA-CB) under the[Master Direction dated 15 September 2025, updated in November 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12896) .


Any company that is not a bank and provides cross-border payment aggregation services will require RBI’s authorisation to operate. A purely technical gateway that does not handle funds is treated differently; check which entity acts as the[payment aggregator](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-aggregators/) in your arrangement.


Once you narrow down your list to international payment gateways, check the[RBI’s list of authorised payment system operators](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/PublicationsView.aspx?id=12043) and ensure that the relevant authorisation covers inward payments. This is the coverage you would want to consider if you are selling to customers outside the country. Match the legal entity on the list with the entity named in your agreement.


##


Step 2: Compare International Payment Gateway Fees on Total Cost


The headline rate doesn’t always reflect the actual cost. Cashfree lists a standard rate of **2.99% per successful international card transaction** , with no setup fee. Currency conversion is applied to the settlement amount. Other providers have other rates, so ask the same questions and expect them to provide you with the answers in writing:


- **Platform fee:** What will you charge for the payment method that your international customers will be using? Identify any separate transaction or instrument charges too.
- **GST:** When asking questions, keep in mind that GST is paid in addition to the fee if the quote is exclusive of GST. Confirm the taxable charges and whether the quote includes it.
- **Currency conversion:** What is the margin for currency conversion, where does the exchange rate come from, and when is it fixed?
- **Additional costs:** Do add-ons come at an extra cost, such as faster settlement, export documents, refunds or dispute handling?


Check the provider’s current rate card and your merchant quote. Cashfree’s[payment gateway charges](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-charges/) distinguish payment methods and platform fees; an advertised offer or enterprise quote may differ from the published standard rate.


Compare the final amount credited for the same customer payment, currency and payment method. A lower headline rate can still leave you with less after FX and other charges.


***Also read:[How to Receive International Business Payments in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-receive-international-business-payments-in-india/)***


##


Step 3: Check International Payment Gateway Settlement Time and Currency


Similar gateways can pay you differently, dependent on how they’re executing their settlements. There are providers who will settle the international payment in INR to your registered bank account within T+2 business days. RBI does not set one universal T+N settlement cycle for cross-border payments. Make sure this is highlighted in the agreement between the aggregator and you, and clearly define the time frame in the agreement.


So negotiate the international payment gateway settlement time in writing; do not leave it to the payment page alone. Ask what “T” means, which days count as business days, and whether cut-offs, reserves or risk reviews can delay a settlement. Your finance team should be able to match transactions to bank credits through[settlement and reconciliation reports](https://www.cashfree.com/settlement-and-reconciliation-guide/) .


The other half is currency. Only Indian exporters directly onboarded by the aggregator facilitating inward payments can settle in a currency other than INR under these directions. Ask the provider if your onboarding process meets the criteria before planning to hold dollars or euros. Confirm that the provider supports the currency and settlement arrangement you need. Collection in a customer’s currency does not automatically mean settlement in that currency.


***Also read:[International Payment Terms for Indian Exporters](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/international-payment-terms/)***


##


Step 4: Check the Export Paperwork


Every export sale must have a paper trail. The payment provider must provide the necessary documents or information to the authorised dealer (AD) bank for closing the corresponding entry in the RBI’s export tracking system, EDPMS, wherever applicable.


These documents are known by different names across providers. Some may issue a Foreign Inward Remittance Statement for each foreign payment. Proof of receipt may also be called a Foreign Inward Remittance Advice or another bank-issued record. A[FIRC, FIRS or FIRA](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/) is not automatically interchangeable with every export-realisation document required for reporting or incentives.


You should also include the appropriate RBI[purpose code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/purpose-code-for-international-payments/) for transactions and maintain receipts. Ask your provider what you’ll be offered and when, and make sure your chartered accountant and AD bank accept it for your export category. Request a sample document before onboarding.


##


Step 5: Check Cross-Border Payment Gateway Features and Limits


The following are some key points that determine the suitability of an international payment gateway:


- **Transaction cap:** RBI limits inward and outward transaction sizes processed through a PA-CB to **₹25 lakh per transaction** . For larger payments, discuss another permitted route with your AD bank. This is not a blanket cap on all international bank transfers.
- **Currency and market coverage:** Some companies offer international coverage in 140+ currencies, with collections from customers around the world, including 170+ countries. Verify that all shortlisted providers support your buyers’ locations, currencies and payment methods.
- **Refunds and disputes:** Customers retain applicable chargeback rights, and refunds are returned to the original payment method unless the payer specifically requests another mode belonging to the same payer. Check the provider’s[refund and chargeback process](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/chargeback-vs-refund-vs-reversal/) , evidence deadlines and charges. RBI also requires an officer and grievance-escalation details to be displayed on the PA’s website.
- **Integration and payment status:** Review the[integration options](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/overview) for your website, app or commerce platform. Check payment-status notifications, refund handling and reporting before going live.
- **Security and customer experience:** Test checkout on a phone, authentication, clear error messages and recovery after a failed payment. For SaaS businesses, verify that recurring international payments are supported for your billing model.


##


International Payment Gateway Checklist: Compare Providers Before Signing


Use the same questions for every provider and retain the answers with your merchant agreement.


**What to compare** **What to confirm in writing**


RBI authorisation Legal entity and relevant inward PA-CB coverage.


Full cost Payment-method charges, GST, FX margin and optional service fees.


Settlement Currency, definition of T, business days, cut-offs and holds.


Export records Document type, issuer, delivery time and AD-bank acceptance.


Limits and coverage ₹25 lakh PA-CB cap, supported markets and permitted business category.


Refunds and support Refund terms, dispute deadlines and escalation contacts.


Integration Successful and failed payment flows, reports and reconciliation.


##

##


FAQs About Choosing an International Payment Gateway


#### 1. What is the single most crucial factor to consider while selecting an international payment gateway?


RBI authorisation. Without it, a non-bank provider would not be allowed to offer cross-border aggregation, and therefore the fees and features would not matter. Check the entity handling your funds and its relevant inward-payment coverage.


#### 2. What does an international payment gateway cost?


This will depend on the provider and payment method. With no setup fee, Cashfree lists a standard rate of 2.99% per successful international card transaction. Check and confirm GST, conversion terms and other applicable charges before signing.


#### 3. What is the time needed for international payment gateway settlement?


This is based on the provider. The time period for settlement is stated as T+2 business days in INR by Cashfree. RBI does not specify a universal time limit; it’s a merchant agreement, so check before you sign it. The agreement must transparently state the timelines. Confirm how holidays, cut-offs and holds are handled.


#### 4. Is it possible to settle an international payment gateway transaction in a foreign currency other than INR?


Only if the aggregator facilitating inward transactions has added you directly as an Indian exporter and supports the required arrangement. Agree this before undertaking foreign-currency settlement.


#### 5. Is there any restriction for a single transaction through an international payment gateway?


Yes. RBI has put a limit of ₹25 lakh on each inward or outward cross-border transaction processed by a PA-CB. Other international transfer routes have their own applicable requirements.
